points.description: States what DHCP is: a network protocol in which a server dynamically assigns IP addresses (and other configuration parameters) to devices/hosts on the network.
points.partial_credit: Half if it only says it is a protocol for IP/network configuration without mentioning dynamic assignment of addresses by a server.

points.description: States what it is used for: simplifying/automating configuration of end systems, e.g. automatic (or manual) IP assignment and supplying extra settings such as DNS server, netmask or default router.
points.partial_credit: Half if the use is only vaguely given (e.g. 'for network setup') without the idea of automatic assignment or extra parameters.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying DHCP is a protocol where a server automatically gives IP addresses (and other settings) to devices, and that it is used to ease or automate host configuration. Give part marks for vague but relevant answers, such as only saying it assigns IP addresses with no mention of use. Mentioning RARP/BOOTP or specific parameters is not required; extra remarks don't lose marks unless they contradict the main idea.
